Power to direct by whom costs are to be paid

[THE UNCLAIMED DEPOSITS ACT, 1870]
[THE UNCLAIMED DEPOSITS ACT, 1870]
(Short
title given by the Short Titles Act, 1897 (14 of 1897).
For Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India,
1870, Pt. V, p 5 ; for Proceedings in Council, see ibid., 1869, Supplement, p.
1506 ; ibid., 1870, Supplement, pp. 53, 57, 92 and 136.)
ACT No. V OF 1870
[4th February, 1870]
An Act to enable
the (Subs.
by A. O., 1949, Sch., for "High Courts at the Presidency‑towns".)[High Court of (Subs. by A. O., 1961, Art. 2 and Sch., for
"East Bengal" (with effect from the 23rd March, 1956).) [East Pakistan]] to deal with cost of
petitions for certain moneys transferred to Government.
1. Power to direct by whom costs are to be paid. Whenever (Subs. ibid., for " any of the said Courts " (with
effect from the 23rd March, 1956).)
[the said Court] shall make an order on any such petition, the Court may direct
by whom the whole or any part of the costs of each party are to be paid.
